Tara — thanks for the clear checklist. Below are concise answers intended for the SIG packet; I have attached a short playbook excerpt and the most recent DR test summary. We can expand any item as needed.

Answers (summary form for SIG):
- RTO / RPO (typical, hosted Redwood API):
  • API control plane + routing: RTO <= 5 minutes (automated routing to healthy region), RPO <= 0 (stateless routing)
  • Model-serving (stateless model containers with warm cache): RTO targeted <= 3 minutes for failover to warm pool; RPO = minutes for in-flight autoretry semantics
  • Embeddings store (managed object store + index): RTO <= 30 minutes for read-only from replica in secondary region; RPO = 15 minutes (async replication)
  • KV-like session cache (in-memory + persistent checkpoint): RTO <= 10 minutes to restore from latest checkpoint; RPO = 5 minutes (checkpoint frequency)

- Backups & retention:
  • Automated daily snapshots for model artifacts and config (retention 30 days).
  • Incremental object backups for embeddings + logs: hourly snapshots retained 7 days, daily retained 30 days, 90-day archival available on request.
  • Immutable object storage in region with cross-region replication to a secondary region for production accounts.

- Cross-region failover:
  • For hosted customers: routing is automated via health checks to alternate region; expected automated failover time 2–10 minutes depending on DNS propagation and sticky sessions.
  • For Dedicated/Private: we provide documented runbook and assistance for failover; can be automated per contract.
  • Validation: post-failover smoke tests (API smoke, token validation, model inference checks) are triggered automatically and reported to ops dashboard.

- DR testing cadence / evidence:
  • Full production failover drill: quarterly (last recorded drill: 2027-04-12). Attached: dr-test-report-202704.pdf (summary of metrics and lessons learned).

- Runbook / playbook: attached excerpt includes stepwise failover checklist, key contacts, and rollback criteria.

Attachments: redwood_bc_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook excerpt), dr-test-report-202704.pdf (summary)

If you want hard numbers for SLA language (e.g., guaranteed RTO windows under Dedicated agreements), Marissa is looping on this message and can confirm contract language or propose an SLA exception.

—Jonas
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Alex — quick clarifications below; attaching the runbook excerpt as plaintext per your request.

1) Embeddings replica topology:
  • Production default: hot-warm replica in secondary region. Reads can be served from the replica with slightly elevated latency; replica is kept 99% caught-up under normal ingestion.
  • Peak ingestion: typical catch-up lag under 200 MB/min is ~2–8 minutes depending on shard distribution. We monitor watermark lag and will throttle ingestion to preserve replication consistency if thresholds are exceeded.

2) KV/session cache consistency & restore guidance:
  • Consistency model: eventual after restore. Checkpoint restores reconstruct the in-memory state from the most recent persisted checkpoint; ongoing in-flight mutations after the checkpoint may be replayed from logs where available but some ephemeral session state may be lost.
  • App guidance: design for idempotent requests and persist critical session state to a durable store (we provide SDK helpers to checkpoint important session keys at shorter intervals).

3) Runbook plaintext snippet attached: redwood_dr_runbook_excerpt.txt (included) — contains step-by-step failover commands, smoke checks, and rollback steps.

We also uploaded the playbook and full test summary to the Drive link included below. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the runbook.

—Jonas
